card.profile: The potato-harvest jumping dance — Huaylas (Huaylarsh) (Peru, Mantaro (Junin)). Full sourced 9-field A+ profile in research artifact W8; concise schema stub pending text expansion.
card.image_significance: The potato-harvest jumping dance. A representative image shows colorful regional costume and lively partner or troupe footwork — Mantaro (Junin), Peru.
card.profile_long: Huaylas, also known as Huaylarsh, is a traditional dance originating from the Mantaro Valley in the Junín department of the central Peruvian Andes. Recognized as a pre-Columbian tradition, the dance is deeply embedded in the agricultural and seasonal cycles of the region. It is historically associated with the potato harvest, serving as a celebration of the land's productivity and the arrival of the rains during the carnival season. The dance is performed by pairs of dancers, specifically referred to as Huaylarsh and wamblas (youths). The choreography is noted for its mimicry of the courtship rituals of birds, characterized by a lively, cheerful, and highly energetic performance style. The dancers engage in vigorous jumping and rhythmic footwork that reflects the vitality of the community. The music accompanying the dance is typically provided by brass bands, which contribute to the festive and loud atmosphere of the performance. The dance is widely practiced in the southern towns of the Huancayo province, including Pucará, Sapallanga, Huancán, Huayucachi, Viques, and Chongos Bajo. As a living tradition, Huaylas continues to be a central expression of cultural identity in the Mantaro Valley, honoring the Pachamama and the fertility of the soil. The dance serves not only as a form of entertainment but as a ritualistic expression of the relationship between the people and their environment, marking the transition of the agricultural calendar. Its endurance as a popular dance form highlights the resilience of Andean traditions in the face of modern cultural shifts, remaining a staple of local festivities and communal gatherings throughout the year.

sections.occasions_and_meaning: The dance is performed in honor of nature, soil fertility, and the arrival of the rains, particularly during the carnival season. It is closely tied to the agricultural cycle of the potato harvest.
sections.regional_variants: The dance is most widely practiced in the southern towns of the Huancayo province, including Pucará, Sapallanga, Huancán, Huayucachi, Viques, and Chongos Bajo.

claims.text: Waylas/Huaylas (Walyash/Huaylarsh, Quechua pronunciation: [ˈwajlas̠]) is a dance from the Mantaro Valley in the department of Junin, in the central Andean part of Peru.
It is a very lively and cheerful dance, characterized by the energy and jumping of the dancers.
It is danced by pairs of dancers.
It originated in association with the potato harvest.
La danse Huaylas est une danse traditionnelle du Pérou d'origine précolombienne, joyeuse et animée originaire des Andes centrales de la vallée du Mantaro, province de Junín.
La danse de couple,est exécutée par les Huaylarsh et les wamblas (jeunes) en l'honneur de la nature, la fertilité des sols, ainsi que l'arrivée des pluies pendant le mois du carnaval.
Habituellement interprété par des groupes et des orchestres de cuivres.
La chorégraphie représente la chute amoureuse des oiseaux.
